Taxonomic work to sort and screen insect samples collected during the season for this project will be conducted by the contracted staff. In addition to sample screening, the taxonomic work also involves preparing voucher specimens and entering data about these vouchers into a database to document. Vouchers involve representatives of both exotic and native species collected during the project. The vouchers will be stored at the FHP, MFO facility and/or the contracted collection room or museum by incorporating them into the insect reference collections that already exist. The expertise provided by the entomologists will be to prepare (pin or point), affix a standard label and a unique number label to each voucher specimen, and systematically arrange it within the collection. 1240BE26Q0101 Morgantown Field Office (MFO) Insect Taxonomy Support Data about the exotic and native species in the orders, families and subfamily, and species listed that were collected will be entered into a reference database developed by the contractor. This information can be used to analyze native and exotic species during this project by MFO. 4.0 Government Furnished Morgantown Field offic

The taxonomist will provide identifications to ensure that field forest health staff are able to provide the most accurate data to land managers. 2.0 Background Morgantown Field Office (MFO) forest health protection staff have worked with cooperators and taxonomist to provide insect identification within the six states and DC footprint of the field office as well as prepare pinned speci

Samples are available for pick-up Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday. Morgantown Field Office 180 Canfield Street, Morgantown, WV 26505 Collection of samples will usually begin in late February and continue until mid-November. However, there may arise an occasion to begin trapping in January and continue until December. The Contractor will begin sorting and identifying the samples from early March and will be given 90 days to finish a sample once delivered. When the last sample is delivered to the Contractor they will have 90 days to complete that sample and deliver the reports and any pinned or curated specimens. Contractor Requirements 3.0 Technical Requirements / Tasks The taxonomist will provide services for the special surveys of woodborers. Fast, accurate screening of raw insect trap samples by highly experienced taxonomists. Small business concern— (1) Means a concern, including its affiliates, that is independently owned and operated, not dominant in its field of operation, and qualified as a small business under the criteria in 13 CFR part 121 and the size standard in paragraph (b) of this provision. (2) Affiliates, as used in this definition, means business concerns, one of whom directly or indirectly controls or has the power to control the others, or a third party or parties control or have the power to control the others. SBA determines affiliation based on the factors set forth at 13 CFR 121.103. The Postbox is an online submission facility which allows buyers to receive responses from suppliers electronically in a secure environment. Responses are submitted through the portal and held in the secure Postbox until the deadline for responses has expired. Nominated members of the buyer organisation then unlock the Postbox to access the submissions. The Postbox can be used for the receipt of PQQs, tender responses, Quick Quote submissions and all supporting documents. A full audit trail is kept of all access to the Postbox and a complete record of all supplier submissions is stored. C.4.4.2 Assessment and Diagnosis. The Contractor shall conduct a comprehensive treatment needs assessment for each client within seven (7) business days of admission. a. Assessment Instrument. The treatment needs assessment shall be conducted using the Addiction Severity Index (ASI) or a comparable, comprehensive biopsychosocial assessment tool. The assessment shall be administered by a qualified staff member meeting the credential requirements set forth in Section C [cross-reference credential section]. The Contractor is not required to administer a new ASI if CSOSA provides an ASI completed within six (6) months of the client's admission date. In such cases, the Contractor shall review the existing ASI, document any clinically significant changes since the prior assessment, and incorporate findings into the initial treatment plan. b. Required Assessment Content. Regardless of the instrument used, the treatment needs assessment shall include, at a minimum, the following: • Substance Use and Treatment History: A detailed account of the client's substance use history, including substances used, patterns and sev

(RSC) Discharge Plan • Community Intervention Team (CIT) assessment • CSOSA Performance Contract • Any prior clinical assessment, psychological evaluation, or treatment summary provided by CSOSA or its designee The Contractor shall not duplicate assessment activities where prior documentation is current and clinically sufficient. Where prior information is incomplete, outdated, or inconsistent with the client's current presentation, the Contractor shall supplement the record accordingly and document the basis for any departure from prior findings. d. Discharge Planning Integration. The initial treatment needs assessment shall reference relevant clinical and psychosocial factors that will inform discharge planning. The Contractor shall identify anticipated discharge needs at the time of assessment, including continuity of care, step-down level of care, housing, behavioral health follow-up, and community support linkages, to support a seamless continuum of care from admission through discharge. e. Documentation and Retention. The completed treatment needs assessment shall be documented in the client's treatment record no later than seven (7) business days following admission. esting, and Preventive Maintenance 1. Project Title GWMP Emergency Generator 2. Agency / Location George Washington Memorial Parkway (GWMP) 3. Objective A; The purpose of this Statement of Work (SOW) is to establish a Base Period plus Four (4) Option Periods contract for the REPLACEMENT of three (3) as like generators for operational readiness of GWMP-owned emergency generators. The Contractor shall replace as like and shall perform inspections, testing, adjustments, and preventive maintenance services to ensure generators remain in a reliable state of readiness to provide uninterrupted emergency power. OR B; The objective of this Statement of Work (SOW) is to establish a Base Period plus Four (4) Option Periods contract for the REPAIR, inspection, preventive maintenance, testing, and operational readiness of existing GWMP-owned emergency generators. The Contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, materials, tools, equipment, and incidental services necessary to ensure all generators remain fully operational and capable of providing uninterrupted emergency power in accordance with manufacturer recommendations, applicable codes, and industry standards. Services shall include routine inspections, testing, adjustments, troubleshooting, preventive maintenance, emergency/after

fter hour repairs, consumable parts and ﬂuids. corrective repairs, replacement of defective or worn components, ongoing operational monitoring, and bi-annual load bank testing to verify system reliability and performance. Non-consumable items, including major parts, components, and equipment requiring repair or replacement outside the scope of routine maintenance, shall be separately priced on an as-needed basis through a Request for Quote (RFQ) issued by the Contracting Officer (CO). Labor costs associated with such repair or replacement services shall be determined in accordance with the pricing established under the contract. 4. Scope of Work The Contractor is responsible to repair/Replace 3 each Generators to serviceable/working conditions to include furnishing all labor, supervision, tools, materials, equipment, transportation, and incidentals necessary to perform preventive maintenance and inspection services on GWMP emergency generator systems. Services shall be performed on a total of 4 generators in accordance with manufacturer guidelines, industry best practices, and applicable codes and regulations. Preventive Maintenance services shall include, but are not limited to, the inspection, testing, adjustment, and servicing of the following generator system components:

separators. • Inspect the entire fuel system for leaks. • Inspect electronic governor connections and actuator operation. • Inspect steel fuel lines for leaks, cracks, and proper support. 4.4 Fuel System – Gaseous (Natural Gas / Propane) • Inspect fuel system for gas leaks. • Inspect ignition system components, including spark plug wires and ignition coils. • Inspect and adjust governor and actuator linkage as required. 4.5 Starting System • Record battery electrolyte speciﬁc gravity for accessible batteries. • Top off electrolyte in lead-acid batteries using distilled water. • Verify and record battery charger and alternator output. • Verify proper cranking termination during startup. • Clean battery terminals and apply corrosion inhibitor as required. • Inspect and tighten battery cable and starter motor connections. 4.6 Exhaust System • Inspect ﬂexible exhaust couplings for cracks, leaks, or missing hardware. • Inspect exhaust manifolds for oil or fuel residue. • Inspect exhaust rain caps and outlet screening. • Drain exhaust moisture traps as required. 4.7 Air Intake System • Inspect air ﬁlters for restriction or deterioration; clean or replace as required (if included). • Inspect intake piping for damage or loose connections. • Inspect air cleaner
